newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Tatung unit to seek US$200 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Tatung unit to seek US$200 mln loan.

text.p: Taiwan's unlisted Chung Hwa Picture Tubes, a subsidiary of electronics giant Tatung, said on Wednesday it was seeking a US$200 million syndicated loan to finance its T$10.5 billion plant in Britain.
"The seven-year US$200 million loan will be used to finance our T$10.5 billion plant in Britain," an executive, who declined to be identified, said by telephone.
The loan, which bears a rate of about LIBOR plus 0.5 percentage point, will include US$100 million in U.S. dollars and 63 million pounds sterling, he said.
Citibank will be the lead underwriter for the loan, he said.
Chung Hwa launched its T$10.5 billion cathode ray tube (CRT) project in 1996 in Britain, he said.
CRTs are key components in producing computer monitors.
Chung Hwa, one of the world's leading CRT makers, is 88.5 percent owned by Tatung, one of the island's biggest electronics and electrical appliance makers.
Chung Hwa also plans to seek a syndicated loan of T$11.6 billion to finance a T$15 billion liquid-crystal display (LCD) project it announced in late 1996, the executive said.
But all other details have yet to be set, he said.
The firm had said it would start construction of the new LCD plant in 1997 in Taiwan to make advanced thin-film-transistor LCDs.
LCDs are a key components for producing notebook computers and monitors.
